Q: Scan directories and delete those that have less than n files A:

This is where I stand, making some progress (I hope) but stuck at penultimate step:

Here, I count songs per album but I can't find a way to sum them up between albums of that same artist.

I'll carefully read the first proposed answer and would welcome your feedback on my attempt :-)

import os #so that I can access files
import shutil #for my shell operations
from pathlib import Path #for source and dest

#variables: my paths and my threshold
source = Path("./music")
dest = Path("./musiclight")
threshold = 3

#I create the dest dir if it doesn't exist
os.makedirs(dest, exist_ok=True)

#variable artist is created and contains each top dir name (artist) (iter makes it a loop)
for artist in source.iterdir():
    if artist.is_dir(): #got from AI, security net to make sure artist is a dir
        #second embedded loop: variable album is created and contains each dir name (album)
        for album in source.iterdir():
            if album.is_dir(): #same security net, now to make sure album a dir
            file_count = sum(1 for f in album.rglob('*') if f.is_file()) #count all the files in that album
            if file_count >= threshold: # idea OK but should happen with sum of songs from all albums, not just this one
            shutil.copytree(artist, dest / artist.name, dirs_exist_ok=True) #should be OK

Q: Why does JSON_VALUE return the object/array as text instead of NULL? A: 
create table events (payload json);
insert into events values ('{"a":1}'), ('[1,2]');

select count(*) from events
where json_value(payload, '$') is null;
-- 0

Same two documents on MySQL 8.4, that count is 2.

MySQL 8.4 also returns 0 - db<>fiddle MySQL 8.4

select count(*) from events
where json_value(payload, '$') is null;
--count(*)
--0

select json_value('42', '$');
-- 42
select json_value('{"a":1}', '$');
-- {"a": 1}
select json_value('[1,2]', '$');
-- [1, 2]

JSON Path Syntax:

As noted previously, in MySQL, the scope of the path is always the document being operated on, represented as $. You can use '$' as a synonym for the document in JSON path expressions.

Searching and Modifying JSON Values ...

Path syntax uses a leading $ character to represent the JSON document under consideration, optionally followed by selectors that indicate successively more specific parts of the document

$ is a valid selector returning the document. {"a": 1} and [1, 2] are not NULLs, therefore count is 0.

Sidenote: Interestingly behavior in question can be observed for MariaDB - db<>fiddle demo MariaDB

Q: Problem when trying to add Prettier's Git Hook: husky install error `install command is deprecated` A:

You are following back dated documentation of Husky

Here is the steps:

  1. Initialize Husky:
pnpm exec husky init
  1. Update your package.json: should look
{
  "scripts": {
    "prepare": "husky"
  }
}
  1. Add Prettier to the pre-commit hook:
echo "pnpm exec lint-staged" > .husky/pre-commit
  1. Add lint-staged configuration to package.json:
"lint-staged": {
  "*.{js,ts,jsx,tsx,json,css,md}": "prettier --write"
}
  1. Verify Git Hook Execution:
  • Make a change
  • git add .
  • git commit -m "test"

Q: JSON_MODIFY is not working properly in SQL Server 2017 A:

This bug appears to be fixed as of SQL Server 2025 RTM. It is not fixed in SQL Server 2022 or earlier, in the latest CU (CU26) as of date of writing.

It was posted three times on the Azure Feedback site, but I could not find any official note on any of them, nor anywhere else, that it was fixed.

Q: Sparse checkout but exclude or ignore files in root? A:

It's possible to use the --no-cone option with git sparse-checkout set to exclude root files in a sparse checkout:

# 1. create the initial sparse clone
git clone --depth 1 --filter=blob:none --sparse <repo/url>

# 2. use '--no-cone' to exclude everything but the wanted dir
git sparse-checkout set --no-cone '/wanted_dir/' '!/*'

With that the root files checked out from step 1 would be removed upon step 2.

See https://git-scm.com/docs/git-sparse-checkout#Documentation/git-sparse-checkout.txt-set
